# Non-opioid analgesics

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Anesthesiology > Drugs > Non-opioid analgesics*

[Original Article Link](/library/BN0zWg)

---

## Summary

Non-<u>opioid</u> <u>analgesics</u> include nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (<u>NSAIDs</u>), selective <u>COX-2</u> inhibitors, and <u>acetaminophen</u>. <u>NSAIDs</u> inhibit <u>cyclooxygenases</u> (<u>COX-1</u> and <u>COX-2</u>), thereby disrupting the production of <u>prostaglandin</u>, an important mediator of <u>pain</u> and inflammation. Consequently, <u>NSAIDs</u> possess <u>antipyretic</u>, <u>analgesic</u>, and anti-inflammatory effects, and are particularly effective in the management of musculoskeletal <u>pain</u> (e.g., rheumatic disorders, inflammatory <u>joint</u> <u>pain</u>). Side effects include <u>gastrointestinal ulcers</u> and bleeding, increased risk of <u>heart</u> attacks, and renal function impairment. The severity of these side effects is often underestimated because most non-<u>opioid</u> <u>analgesics</u> are easily available <u>OTC</u>. Selective <u>COX-2</u> inhibitors have similar effects to <u>NSAIDs</u>, but show a lower risk for gastrointestinal side effects. <u>Acetaminophen</u> possesses <u>antipyretic</u> and <u>analgesic</u> effects and is the most commonly used over-the-counter (<u>OTC</u>) <u>oral analgesic</u> drug. It is generally well tolerated, but <u>acetaminophen overdose</u> can result in significant <u>hepatotoxicity</u> with the risk of <u>acute liver failure</u>.

## Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

### Agents




* <u>Ibuprofen</u>

* <u>Diclofenac</u>

* <u>Indomethacin</u>

* <u>Naproxen</u>

* <u>Piroxicam</u>

* <u>Meloxicam</u>

* <u>Ketorolac</u>

* <u>Sulindac</u>

* <u>Aspirin</u>





### Mechanism of action




* Reversible inhibition of the enzymes <u>COX-1</u> and <u>COX-2</u> → decreased <u>prostaglandin</u> synthesis

* <u>Aspirin</u> is the exception, because it leads to irreversible <u>COX-1</u> and <u>COX-2</u> inhibition. (See <u>aspirin</u> for more information.)





### Effects




* <u>Analgesic</u>

* <u>Antipyretic</u>

* Anti-inflammatory (antirheumatic)

* Minor antiplatelet function (with the exception of <u>aspirin</u>)





### Side effects




* Gastric and <u>duodenal ulcers</u> with the risk of <u>gastrointestinal bleeding</u> and perforation (inhibition of <u>COX</u> disrupts the production of protective gastric <u>mucosal</u> <u>prostaglandins</u>) 

* Risk increases with duration and dose of treatment  [[2]](/library/qK0ChS)[[3]](/library/g90F5R)

* Prophylaxis: 

* Administration of <u>proton pump inhibitors</u> (in case long-term intake is needed) [[4]](/library/36bSku)

* See “<u>Prevention of NSAID-induced GI toxicity</u>” for details.

* Increased risk for <u>diverticulitis</u> and <u>diverticular bleeding</u>

* Increased risk of <u>heart attack</u> and <u>stroke</u>  (with the exception of <u>aspirin</u> and <u>naproxen</u>) [[5]](/library/S90y5R)

* Renal function impairment: <u>Prostaglandins</u> normally maintain <u>renal blood flow</u> by inducing <u>vasodilation</u> of the <u>afferent arterioles</u>. NSAIDS inhibit <u>prostaglandin</u> production, which leads to harmful <u>hypoperfusion</u> of the <u>kidneys</u> and reduced <u>GFR</u>. ;  [[6]](/library/elYxD6)

* <u>Electrolyte</u> and fluid abnormalities (<u>edema</u>, <u>hyperkalemia</u>, <u>hyponatremia</u>)

* Worsening of <u>hypertension</u>

* In rare cases, <u>acute renal failure</u>

* <u>Analgesic nephropathy</u>: prolonged <u>NSAID</u> use results in <u>tubulointerstitial nephritis</u> and <u>papillary necrosis</u> (↑ crea/<u>BUN</u> <u>ratio</u>, slight ↑ <u>K<sup>+</sup></u>)  [[7]](/library/h90cMR)

* <u>Aplastic anemia</u> [[8]](/library/S6by4u)

* <u>Pseudoallergic reactions</u>  [[9]](/library/h6bcku)

* <u>Urticaria</u> and <u>angioedema</u>

* <u>Asthma</u>

* <u>Aspirin</u>-exacerbated respiratory disease (<u>AERD</u>)

* For side effects of <u>aspirin</u>, see <u>aspirin</u>.





> [!WARNING]
> The risk of an <u>ulcer</u> is 10–15 times higher if NSAIDS and <u>glucocorticoids</u> are administered simultaneously!




![Effects of NSAIDs and ACEIs on renal filtration](media/ayeytgxykunozokzvdi2bjs9.jpg)

Effects of NSAIDs and ACEIs on renal filtration




### Indications




* Acute and <u>chronic pain</u> (particularly musculoskeletal)

* <u>Rheumatoid arthritis</u>

* Inflammatory <u>arthritis</u>

* <u>Kawasaki disease</u>

* <u>Acute gout</u> attack

* Post-operative <u>pain</u>

* Dysmenorrhoea

* <u>Headache</u>, <u>migraine</u>

* <u>Fever</u>

* <u>Indomethacin</u>: closure of a <u>patent ductus arteriosus</u>

* See <u>aspirin</u> for specific indications of <u>aspirin</u>.





### Contraindications




Contraindications for NSAIDs include:




* <u>Gastroduodenal ulcers</u>

* Acute hemorrhage (especially <u>aspirin</u>)

* <u>Renal failure</u>

* Recent <u>myocardial infarction</u>, <u>unstable angina</u>, <u>heart failure</u>

* <u>Surgery</u>: discontinue <u>NSAIDs</u> 1–3 days prior to <u>surgery</u>

* Avoid <u>NSAIDs</u> during <u>pregnancy</u>!





> [!WARNING]
> <u>NSAIDs</u> are contraindicated in the second and <u>third trimester</u> as they may cause premature <u>closure of the ductus arteriosus</u>. Furthermore, they can inhibit uterine contractility.




References:[[2]](/library/qK0ChS)[[10]](/library/IK0Y3S)[[11]](/library/ghYFWK)

## Selective COX-2 inhibitors

### Agent



* Celecoxib  [[12]](/library/P90WnR)




### Mechanism of action




* Reversible selective inhibition of <u>COX-2</u> with almost no inhibition of <u>COX-1</u>

* <u>COX-2</u> is found in:

* Cells that mediate inflammation and <u>pain</u> (e.g., <u>macrophages</u>, <u>leukocytes</u>)

* Vascular <u>endothelial</u> cells (i.e., cells that control <u>vasodilation</u>)





### Effects




* <u>Analgesic</u> and anti-inflammatory

* Advantages in comparison to <u>nonselective NSAIDs</u>

* No antiplatelet effect: <u>platelets</u> only possess <u>COX-1</u> and are therefore not targeted by selective <u>COX-2</u> inhibitors. This means that the activity of <u>thromboxane A<sub>2</sub></u> (<u>TXA<sub>2</sub></u>) is not interrupted (<u>TXA<sub>2</sub></u> normally promotes <u>platelet aggregation</u>).

* Gastric <u>mucosal</u> cells express mostly <u>COX-1</u>, which is involved in maintaining a healthy gastric <u>mucosa</u>, so there are minimal gastrointestinal side effects and a lower risk of <u>gastric ulcers</u>.





### Side effects




* Increased risk of <u>thrombosis</u>, <u>MI</u>, and/or <u>stroke</u>

* <u>Sulfa drug</u> <u>allergic reaction</u>

* Renal side effects in at-risk patients 

* Deterioration of <u>chronic renal failure</u>

* Worsening of <u>hypertension</u>





### Indications




* <u>Rheumatoid arthritis</u>, <u>osteoarthritis</u>, <u>acute pain</u>, nonrheumatoid <u>joint</u> <u>pain</u>

* Especially as an alternative to <u>nonselective NSAIDs</u> for patients with a history of <u>peptic ulcer disease</u> and <u>platelet disorders</u> (e.g., <u>Glanzmann thrombasthenia</u>)





### Contraindications




* Severe <u>heart failure</u>, recent <u>myocardial infarction</u>, <u>gastrointestinal bleeding</u>

* <u>Sulfa drug</u> <u>allergy</u>





> [!NOTE]
> “sele<u>COX</u>ib:” <u>celecoxib</u> is a selective <u>COX-2</u> inhibitor.




References:[[12]](/library/P90WnR)[[13]](/library/XC09qR)

## Other non-opioid analgesics

### Agent



* Acetaminophen




### Mechanism of action




* Reversibly inhibits <u>cyclooxygenase</u>, mainly in the <u>CNS</u>

* Inactivated peripherally





### Effects




* <u>Antipyretic</u>

* <u>Analgesic</u>

* No anti-inflammatory effect





### Side effects




* Minimal gastric side effects

* <u>APAP-induced hepatotoxicity</u>

* <u>Acute liver failure</u> can occur with <u>acetaminophen overdose</u>.





### Indications



* <u>Fever</u> and <u>pain</u>

* Good tolerability

* Preferred <u>analgesic</u>/<u>antipyretic</u> drug during <u>pregnancy</u>

* Preferred over <u>aspirin</u> in pediatric viral infections because it has a lower risk of causing <u>Reye syndrome</u>




### Contraindications



* Severe <u>liver</u> impairment




> [!NOTE]
> Maximum daily dose of <u>acetaminophen</u>: 4 g (adults).
> References:[[13]](/library/XC09qR)
